'''Fyodor Dmitriyevich Gakhov''' ({{langx|ru|Фёдор Дмитриевич Гахов}}; 19 February 1906, [[Cherkessk]] — 30 March 1980, [[Minsk]]) was a Soviet and Russian [[mathematician]] and a specialist in the field of boundary value problems for analytic functions of a [[Complex analysis|complex variable]].
== Biography ==
Fyodor Dmitriyevich Gakhov was born on 19 February 19 1906 in Batalpashinskaya village (present-day [[Cherkessk]], [[Stavropol Krai]]) in the family of a shoemaker. His father died when he was a boy. After graduating from the Circassian Pedagogical College in 1925, he entered [[North Ossetian State University|Gorsky Pedagogical Institute]] in [[Vladikavkaz]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://50.uginfo.sfedu.ru/jzl.htm|title=Юбилей ЮГИНФО ЮФУ \\ Жизнь замечательных людей|website=50.uginfo.sfedu.ru|access-date=2018-05-16}}</ref>

In 1928, on the recommendation of Professor L. I. Kreer, he was admitted to [[Kazan Federal University]], which he graduated in 1930.<ref name=":1" />

In 1934—1937 Fyodor Gakhov taught [[mathematics]] at the universities of [[Yekaterinburg|Sverdlovsk]], and alter enrolled in the graduate school of Kazan University, where his scientific guide was [[Boris Gagaev]]. He decided to specialize on the solution of boundary value problems in the theory of analytic functions and the corresponding integral integral equations.<ref name=":1" />

In 1937 Gakhov defended his [[Candidate of Sciences]] thesis "''Linear boundary value problems in the theory of [[Analytic function|analytic functions]]''". This work was awarded the second prize at the All-Union competition of works of young scientists. From 1937 to 1939 he worked as an [[assistant professor]] at the Kazan University, and from 1939 to 1947 he was the head of the Department of Mathematical Analysis of the [[North Ossetian State University|North Ossetian Pedagogical Institute]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://nasb.gov.by/rus/members/academicians/gakhov.php|title=Академик ГАХОВ Фёдор Дмитриевич}}</ref>

In 1943 he defended his [[Doctor of Sciences]] thesis "''Boundary value problems in the theory of analytic functions and singular integral equations''". In 1943 he became a [[professor]].<ref name=":1" />

In 1947—1953 years Gakhov worked as a professor, and later as head of the Department of Differential Equations of Kazan University. In 1953—1961 he headed the Department of Differential Equations of [[Rostov State University]].<ref name=":0" />

From 1961 until his death Gakhov worked at [[Belarusian State University]]. There he headed the Department of Mathematical Analysis, then the Department of Theory of Functions and Functional Analysis, and later worked as a professor in the Department of Theory of Functions. In 1962—1963 years he was Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics. In 1966 Gakhov was elected a full member of the Academy of Sciences of the Byelorussian SSR.<ref name=":0" />

Fyodor Gakhov died on 30 March 1980 and was buried at the Northern Cemetery of [[Minsk]].<ref name=":1" />

He was the author of the famous monograph "''Boundary Problems''", where he presented the results on solution of [[Riemann–Hilbert problem|Riemann-Hilbert problem]], which he studied together with a group of students. This work has been translated to [[English language|English]]<ref>''Gakhov, F. D.'' Boundary value problems. Pergamon Press, Oxford, 1966.</ref><ref>''Gakhov, F. D.'' Boundary value problems. Dover, New York, 1990, 561 p. — {{isbn|9780486662756}}</ref> and [[Spanish language|Spanish]].<ref>''Gakhov, F. D.'' Problemas de Contorno. Mir. Moscú, 1980.</ref>
